figures.finding: California and New York both hold a person a minor until eighteen: California's Family Code section 6500 and New York's Domestic Relations Law section 2.
figures.applies: US.CA: Family Code s. 6500 (read through california.public.law, which names the Legislature's leginfo page; leginfo answered a Cloudflare challenge). US.NY: Domestic Relations Law s. 2 defines minor for that chapter; Arts and Cultural Affairs Law s. 35.03 and Labor Law s. 150 use 'infant' and 'child performer' (under eighteen) for the contract and permit rules.

sources.said: A minor is an individual who is under 18 years of age.
is a person under the age of eighteen years.

figures.finding: In California a minor's contract for artistic or creative services, expressly including writing, directing and producing, can't be disaffirmed once the superior court approves it, and the court must order 15% of gross earnings set aside by the employer into a Coogan trust; in New York a performer's contract may be approved by the Supreme or Surrogate's Court, and every child performer's employer, writers, directors and producers included, must transfer 15% of gross earnings to a child performer trust account.

US.CA.binding: approval by the superior court (Family Code 6751); otherwise disaffirmable before majority or within a reasonable time after (6710)

setAside.into: Coogan trust account (Family Code 6753); to The Actors' Fund of America if no trustee statement within 180 days

US.NY.binding: approval by the supreme court or surrogate's court (Arts and Cultural Affairs Law 35.03), for performing artists only; the court may set aside up to half of net earnings

setAside.into: child performer trust account (EPTL 7-7.1); to the state comptroller's holding fund if none is notified within 15 days

figures.applies: Unemancipated minors under eighteen. California's chapter covers contracts made on or after 1 January 2000. New York's court approval covers performing services only; its 15% trust follows the Labor Law's wider 'artistic or creative services'.

figures.finding: Federal child-labour law exempts child actors and performers in film, theatre, radio and television (writers and directors aren't named); California's Labor Commissioner issues an entertainment work permit to every minor from 15 days to 18 and caps time on set and at work by age, with a studio teacher and parent; New York's Department of Labor issues a one-year child performer permit, which reaches writers, directors and producers, with its own age table.

federal.exempt: child employed as an actor or performer in motion pictures, theatrical, radio or television productions
federal.otherRoles: general 16 (14 for permitted occupations) minimum of 29 CFR 570.2

US.CA.permit: Entertainment Work Permit and employer's Permit to Employ, issued by the Labor Commissioner (DLSE)
US.CA.timesOfDay: 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.; to 12:30 a.m. before a non-school day
US.CA.studioTeacher: one per 10 or fewer minors (6 months to 16) on school days, 20 on non-school days

US.NY.permit: child performer permit, issued by the Department of Labor, valid one year; employer's certificate of eligibility
US.NY.timesOfDay: not before 5:00 a.m.; non-live 6-17 no later than 10:00 p.m. before school days, 12:30 a.m. on non-school mornings
US.NY.instruction: average 3 hours per school day, with a certified teacher

figures.applies: Federal: the Fair Labor Standards Act's child labour rules. California and New York as the two main production states; other states not read here.

sources.said: any child employed as an actor or performer in motion pictures or theatrical productions, or in radio or television productions.
sets a general 16-year minimum age which applies to all employment subject to its child labor provisions in any occupation other than in agriculture

Minors aged 15 days to 18 years employed in the entertainment industry must have a permit to work, and employers must have a permit to employ, both permits being issued by the Labor Commissioner's Office .

Minors who have reached the age of nine (9) years but who have not attained the age of sixteen (16) years may be permitted at the place of employment for a maximum of nine (9) hours. Such nine (9)-hour period shall consist of not more than five (5) hours of work and at least three (3) hours of schooling when the minor's school is in session.
Twelve (12) hours must elapse between the minor's time of dismissal and time of call on the following day.

Minors in the entertainment industry may not work more than eight hours in a day [LC 1308.7 and 1392] or more than 48 hours in a week. [LC 1308.7] They may only work between the hours of 5 a.m. and 10 p.m. (to 12:30 a.m. on days preceding a non-school- day).
All minors aged 6 months to 16 years must be provided with one studio teacher for each group of ten or fewer minors when school is in session
Employment permits for child performers shall be valid for one year from the date of issuance.
"Child performer" shall mean any child under the age of eighteen who (a) resides in the state of New York and who agrees to render artistic or creative services
Child performers must receive 12 hours of rest between workdays.
Teachers must provide instruction for an average of at least three hours per school day on a weekly basis.
A Responsible Person must be designated to monitor the activity and safety of each child performer under the age of 16 at the work place.

figures.finding: Delaware's corporation law requires each director to be a natural person and states no minimum age in s. 141(b); California's Corporations Code wasn't read.
figures.applies: Delaware General Corporation Law s. 141(b); the age at which a minor may sign the papers or hold shares isn't stated there.

sources.said: The board of directors of a corporation shall consist of 1 or more members, each of whom shall be a natural person.

figures.finding: The Writers Guild of America admits by units of writing employment or sales with signatory companies (24 units in three years for current membership, fewer for associate membership) and states no age.
figures.applies: WGA West's Join the Guild page, read 2026-11-01.

sources.said: We work on a unit system (described in detail below*) based on writing employment and/or sales within the Guild's jurisdiction and with a "signatory" company (a company that has signed the Guild's collective bargaining agreement). … Current membership: In order to be eligible for Current membership a writer must acquire a minimum of 24 units in the three years preceding application.

figures.finding: The federal arts endowment's Grants for Arts Projects in media arts go only to US non-profit organisations, governments and tribes with three years of arts programming; individuals and for-profit companies are not eligible, so a young filmmaker reaches it only through a non-profit.
figures.applies: NEA FY2025 Grants for Arts Projects, Media Arts webinar slides (arts.gov); later years not checked.
